text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Danish State Rail(DSB) has transported 1.2 million Danes over the new Great Belt tunnel/bridge fixed link which opened in June between Denmark's two biggest islands at the mouth of the Baltic. This has meant major passenger losses for Odense and Aarhus airports in central and western Denmark.

--Transparency International, a German-based non-governmental organisation, rates Denmark as the world's most honest country, followed closely by Finland and Sweden, Nigeria has the dubious honour of being judged the world's most corrupt nation.
--France Telecom's Mobilix subsidiary is to have its own telephony network when it opens services in Denmark in competition with Tele Danmark and work on putting cables down has begun.
--Unidanmark, Denmark's second biggest bank, is short of 135 million crowns to fulfil its savings plan target, implying that its efficiency drive has not met expectations.
--Leading Liberal and Conservative opposition parties are to coordinate efforts to campaign for a Danish 'yes' to the European Union's Amsterdam treaty reforms in next year's referendum in Denmark.
--Denmark's biggest firms lag behind major foreign competitors as regards earnings growth, a new survey shows.
